source: APPETITE_GUIDELINES.pdf, 2025 Sample: Commercial Property Underwriting Guidelines
assumptions: Weights, 70% credit for acceptable-but-not-target values, and score caps are project choices, not carrier-prescribed math.
Primary risk state uses the state with the greatest insured building TIV; ties or incomplete exposures require review. Headquarters is not a risk-state substitute.

Construction mix is weighted by building TIV. The guideline names Joisted Masonry, non-combustible/steel, and masonry non-combustible. ISO Class 5-6 (Modified Fire Resistive, Fire Resistive) are treated as acceptable because their fire performance is superior to every class the guideline names; this is a documented interpretation and is labelled as such on each affected submission.

Every insured building must satisfy the year rule; the oldest building determines age credit. Roof updates do not replace year built, but a roof year later than the original build is surfaced as mitigating context.
Total premium sums policies explicitly linked to the submission. Target premium and requested limit are not substitutes for premium or TIV.
Loss value is incurred indemnity plus expenses (paid plus reserves) for property claims on the same insured during the five years before the proposed effective date.

Five-year loss history is scored on how much of the window is actually covered by property policies on file. Uncovered periods are reported as explicit date ranges to request from the prior carrier rather than being treated as loss-free.
Exactly 1990, exactly $100,000 loss, and exactly 50% acceptable construction require review because the guideline does not resolve those boundaries.
Monetary thresholds are interpreted as USD. Missing or other currencies require review; no exchange-rate conversion is applied.

External evidence captured from public sources is advisory only. It can corroborate or contradict a Federato value, but it never by itself satisfies an appetite factor without underwriter confirmation.
All submissions remain visible, including non-property lines and submissions without linked policies. Decisions are triage recommendations, not binding policy actions.
